attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post, given as his own conclusion after summarising the complaint. It is not a quotation of Musk.

semantics.note: Faithful. It is an unhedged retrospective judgment that the organization Musk supported was not what he got. The tone is evaluative, but read in context it is an observation about OpenAI's mission and structure.

contract.note: The plain reading compares the commitments tied to Musk's support with OpenAI as of March 2024, allowing for changes Musk agreed to. That is an ordinary, fair reading. Marcus named no specific term, so the result depends on how commitments and agreed changes are construed.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own account (company disclosure). It says Musk accepted that the mission did not require open-sourcing AGI. This is partial counterevidence on openness only, and it is not an independent finding.

OpenAI's 2019 description of OpenAI LP (company disclosure). It shows a commercial arm under nonprofit control with capped returns. It documents a change but does not settle whether the change broke commitments to Musk.

The court's account of the discovery record. It shows renewed nonprofit assurances to Musk, his continued donations, and a term sheet he got but never answered. It also notes the dispute over disclosure, so whether the commitments were fulfilled stays open.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows that nonprofit assurances were given to Musk and that OpenAI later restructured. OpenAI disputes the openness commitment, and e3 records disputes over what Musk was told and accepted. Nothing in the packet establishes either an unfulfilled commitment that Musk did not agree to change, or fulfillment or agreement. So neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.
